newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian stock market value soared 29 pct in Q1.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian stock market value soared 29 pct in Q1.

text.p: Aggregate market capitalisation of listed equities on the Nigerian bourse grew by 28.68 percent in the first quarter of 1997 from the last quarter of 1996, the market regulator said on Thursday.
In its latest quarterly report , the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) said market capitalisation hit 360 billion naira at end-March 1997 from 279.78 billion naira by end-December 1996.
"The increase could be attributed to the continued appreciation of share prices," it said.
Market analysts said on Thursday that they expected the second quarter's figures to show a downturn following recent drop in share prices.

The market capitalisation for all the quoted equities on Wednesday stood at 377.03 billion naira. The combined market capitalisation of the top 20 quoted equities rose by 31.50 percent in the same period, touching 281.7 billion naira from 214.2 billion naira.
SEC said the top 20 firms accounted for 78.24 percent of the total market value of equities listed on the exchange.
PZ Industries, valued at 29.767 billion naira by end-March, was the market's most capitalised firm.
Some 182 firms are quoted on the Nigerian stock exchange daily official list, among which 19 are on the second-tier securities market set up to encourage small companies to enter the capital market.
